purpose: Record what the Levels 1-9 benchmark is actually taught by reader-visible material, separately from what the scope matrix's anchors imply. The two numbers differ, and the difference is the point of this file.

truthBoundary.structural: structuralAnchoredTargets counts atomic targets whose scope topic names at least one anchor module that is currently reader-visible. It is a graph property. It does NOT establish that the anchored module teaches the target: a Level 6 topic anchored to M30 counts as anchored even though M30 contains no inference algorithm.
truthBoundary.reviewed: reviewedDelivery is a dated human judgement about whether reader-visible material teaches the section at all. Where it says 'none', the absenceProbes below make the claim machine-checkable: every probe term must be absent from reader-visible modules, so the claim fails loudly if material is later added without updating this record.
truthBoundary.nonClaim: Neither number establishes learner mastery, module quality, or release readiness.

levels.label: Mathematical foundations
levels.undeliveredBecause: Optimization and information theory are authored in M31, which is hidden. Martingales, Markov chains, sufficient statistics, and exponential families are thin or absent in M30.

levels.label: Core computer science
levels.undeliveredBecause: Theory of computation is authored in M33, which is hidden. No lower-level language (C, C++, Rust) is taught anywhere, and the NumPy/PyTorch/JAX/GPU material sits in the hidden M32.

recordedDecisions.target: At least one lower-level language, preferably C, C++, or Rust
recordedDecisions.note: The benchmark says 'master'; the course's own scope matrix sets l2.programming-lower-level-ml-runtime to scoped-exposure with capabilities recognize/read/debug/design and no implement. M32 teaches reading a native buffer descriptor, not writing C, C++, or Rust. This is a chosen ceiling, not an oversight, and the absence probes above keep it honest. Raising it needs either an implement-level section in M32 or a dedicated module; that is a curriculum decision, not an editing task.

levels.label: Classical artificial intelligence
levels.undeliveredBecause: M10 supplies graph search and M30 supplies decision-theoretic probability, but A*, admissible heuristics, CSPs, planning, resolution, and POMDPs are authored in M34, which is hidden.

levels.label: Core machine learning
levels.undeliveredBecause: M30 supplies estimation, likelihood, and evaluation discipline. Model families and representation learning are authored in M35 and learning theory in M36, both hidden.

levels.label: Deep learning
levels.undeliveredBecause: No module, hidden or visible, teaches backpropagation derivation, architecture families, or modern training methodology. Closing this level requires new authoring (planned M37-M39).

levels.label: Probabilistic modeling and inference
levels.undeliveredBecause: The scope matrix anchors every Level 6 topic to M30 and M31, but no reader-visible module contains an inference algorithm. This is the clearest case where the structural number is misleading: 16 of 16 targets are anchored and 0 are taught.

levels.label: Sequential decision-making and reinforcement learning
levels.undeliveredBecause: M11 supplies dynamic programming as an algorithm-design paradigm, which is why targets appear anchored, but no reader-visible module teaches Bellman equations for MDPs, value or policy iteration, or any learning method.

levels.label: Foundation models, LLMs, and generative AI
levels.undeliveredBecause: Targets appear anchored through M22, M25, and M26 because those modules discuss evaluation, security, and agent oversight in general terms. No reader-visible module teaches tokenization for language models, transformer internals, pretraining, preference learning, or retrieval-augmented generation.

levels.label: Deep specialization: NLP and language models
levels.undeliveredBecause: Every target is anchored through M20, M23, M25, and M35, but the only 'parsing' in reader-visible material is programming-language parsing in M23. No linguistic structure, translation, sequence labeling, or dialogue material exists.
